name: Cover Bonus Grid
description: Directional cover, computed from the map, applied to the shot. Standing adjacent to a wall on the attacker's side makes the shot harder; the bonus belongs to the defender and flips with attack direction, which is exactly why cover is computed per attack instead of stored per tile — a tile is not 'in cover', a shot is. world.tile_grid supplies the geometry and combat.damage_resolver applies the final number; this component's whole job is the modifier in between, and it never touches damage directly, so a tactics game and a tactics-adjacent RPG share one resolver. Half cover versus full cover is data on the tile, not a special case in code.

implementations.note: Implemented in the consuming application; not verifiable from this repository.

inputs.name: halfCoverMultiplier
inputs.description: Incoming hit-chance or damage scale past half cover. 0.8 makes cover meaningful without making it a wall.

inputs.name: fullCoverMultiplier
inputs.description: Scale past full cover. 0.5 is the strong statement: full cover halves the problem, flanking deletes it.

inputs.name: coverTags
inputs.description: Tile feature tags that grant cover, as data, so level designers add cover objects without code.

inputs.name: flankingIgnoresCover
inputs.description: Whether attacks from an uncovered side bypass the bonus. True is what makes cover a positioning puzzle instead of a stat.

outputs.name: lastCoverAssessment
outputs.description: Direction, tier, and multiplier of the most recent shot evaluated.
